tagline: Leading thin-film PV solar technology and manufacturing company in the Western Hemisphere
hero_kpi_rationale: Robust growth of 24% to $5.2 Bn in 2025, reflecting the acceleration of global solar energy deployment and strong demand for U.S.-manufactured photovoltaic modules

kpis.name: Net Sales
kpis.explanation: Total revenue generated by the company
kpis.description: FSLR's net sales increased by 24% in 2025 compared to 2024, rising from $4.2 Bn to $5.2 Bn, primarily driven by higher volumes of modules sold to third parties

kpis.name: Gross Margin
kpis.explanation: Gross margin as a percentage of net sales
kpis.description: Gross margin decreased by 360 basis points to 40.6% in 2025 from 44.2% in 2024, primarily due to higher costs of U.S.-manufactured modules, warehousing expenses, tariffs, and logistics fees
kpis.signal: Decline in gross margin due to U.S. production costs

kpis.name: Module Production Volume
kpis.explanation: Photovoltaic module production capacity in gigawatts
kpis.description: FSLR produced 16.1 GW of solar modules in 2025 and sold 17.5 GW

risks.title: Regulatory Risk
risks.score_rationale: The company is highly dependent on advanced manufacturing tax credits under the Inflation Reduction Act (IRA). Legislative or regulatory changes could materially reduce these financial benefits

risks.title: Pricing Competition Risk
risks.score_rationale: The solar industry is characterized by intense pricing competition, with numerous Chinese competitors having access to sovereign capital or forms of government support, which could compress margins

risks.title: Foreign Currency Exchange Risk
risks.score_rationale: The company's subsidiaries in multiple countries have cash flows denominated in currencies other than their functional currency, exposing the company to foreign exchange risks

risks.title: Supply Chain Risk
risks.score_rationale: The company has a global manufacturing footprint spanning the U.S., India, Malaysia, and Vietnam, making it vulnerable to supply chain disruptions and trade tariffs

risks.title: Customer Concentration Risk
risks.score_rationale: In 2025, the company terminated supply agreements with BP Solar and Lightsource, resulting in $384.6 M in termination payments and a legal action for recovery

risks.title: Manufacturing Capacity Expansion Risk
risks.score_rationale: The company is building its sixth manufacturing plant in the U.S., scheduled to begin operations in the second half of 2026, which carries risks of delays and cost overruns

ai_positioning.summary: First Solar recognizes the growing demand for energy capacity driven by AI-powered data centers, which are increasing overall electric load and utility-scale solar energy demand, but is not developing any AI-specific products or services.
evidence: utility and corporate demand for energy and overall electric load growth, especially as a result of AI-driven data center demand, continue to increase
